extracted.intended_audience: researchers, scientometricians, NIH policymakers and grant reviewers interested in the predictive validity of peer review scores
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating how well NIH peer-review percentile scores (and component review criteria) predict subsequent grant productivity using bibliometric outcomes (citations, publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation counts of grant-supported publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary bibliometric outcome for grant productivity. The study finds weak predictive power of percentile scores for citation counts within the funded range; note that citations are an imperfect proxy for productivity (see methodological note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of publications acknowledging the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of publications that explicitly acknowledge the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a productivity measure distinct from citation impact; part of the study's outcome set for assessing predictive validity of review scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median citations per publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Median number of citations across publications attributed to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures central tendency of citation impact per paper; one of multiple bibliometric outcomes used to evaluate predictive validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum citations to top paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum citation count received by the single most-cited paper from the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures extreme/high-impact outcomes; useful because some grants produce one highly influential paper rather than many moderately cited ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation rate normalized by field, year, and article type
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation rate adjusted/normalized for field, publication year, and article type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization addresses baseline differences across fields and time; included to reduce confounding when using citations as a productivity metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation productivity above the median (binary outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a grant's citation productivity exceeds the median (binary outcome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a discrimination test; study reports AUC = 0.54 (95% CI: 0.53–0.54) for predicting this outcome from percentile scores — only marginally better than chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH percentile score (aggregate reviewer ranking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentile scores that aggregate reviewer judgments to rank applications relative to peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary predictor examined. Findings: percentile scores have only weak ability to predict bibliometric productivity within the funded range; discrimination is slightly better across the full percentile range but 'collapses to near-random' in the 3rd–20th percentile (the typical fundable zone). The study concludes fine-grained percentile distinctions are not statistically defensible in the fundable zone and gives reform options (e.g., lottery or alternate success metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the project addresses an important problem or barrier to progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the component review dimensions aggregated into the percentile score. The study reports that Significance, individually or combined with other dimensions, does not reliably predict subsequent citation productivity within the fundable range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the qualifications, experience, and track record of the PI(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard component of NIH review. The study finds Investigator scores do not reliably predict bibliometric productivity among funded grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the project employs novel concepts, approaches, or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in NIH scoring; according to the analysis, Innovation scores do not meaningfully predict later citation-based productivity within the fundable range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed to accomplish project aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central review dimension; the paper reports that Approach scores fail to reliably predict subsequent bibliometric outcomes among funded grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional support, resources, and institutional environment for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another component of NIH review; like the other dimensions, Environment scores were not predictive of citation productivity within the fundable range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical defensibility of fine-grained percentile distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether small differences in percentile rankings within the fundable zone are statistically meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper asserts that fine-grained distinctions (e.g., small percentile differences within the fundable zone) are not statistically defensible given weak predictive signal; implication: rubrics that produce an illusion of precision should be reconsidered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of random selection/lottery within fundable range
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt lottery or random selection among applications judged fundable when differences are indistinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as one policy/rubric design implication: if reviewer-based distinctions are essentially indistinguishable in the fundable range, a lottery may be a defensible alternative to fine-grained ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define/measure success metrics other than citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose alternative success metrics beyond citation-based bibliometrics for evaluating grant outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study recommends considering other outcome measures (e.g., training outcomes, knowledge translation) because citations may not capture all dimensions of grant success and percentile scores might predict some non-bibliometric outcomes better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: citations are an imperfect proxy for grant productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that citation metrics do not fully capture the value or outputs of funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological caveat noted by authors: citations miss many dimensions (e.g., training, translation), high-risk grants can have high variance, and reliance on citation-based rubrics may misrepresent true productivity.
